title: Transient model API errors are retried a bounded number of times, other model errors never, and the supervisor is told once
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/recover.rs, the module comment, `Cause`/`Path`, `Turn::cause`, `classify`, `pending` and `next_fact`, `interrupt_turn`, `interrupt_end`, `wait_path`, `revive` and `failed_resumes` (how an interruption is recorded, waited on and revived today); docs/fleet-architecture.md's recovery table (`model_unavailable`, `model_auth`, the paths) and §9 "Not built" ("retrying after a transient API error"); crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs (`Why`, `Escalation::tag`, `Why::is_news`, the host items read from records) and dispatch/digest.rs (`hold_expiries`: a record told once by its tag); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql `spawn_host_record` (the interruption causes and paths it accepts); rsi/scenarios/028.sh (the recovery scenario, whose checks must stay green).

The problem. A worker's engine that ends on the model API's error is handled two ways today, both wrong for an unattended fleet. A transient error (429, 500, 503, 529, `overloaded`, `rate_limit`, `server_error`) is retried after the model backoff, the ended engine resumed in its native session, for as long as it keeps failing: an account that is out for hours resumes the worker forever and nobody is told. Any other model error (a 400 such as an invalid request, a 404, a 413) is no cause at all, so the engine's end after it is classified `crashed` and resumed at once, again and again, though the same request fails the same way every time. The supervisor is told of neither.

Required behaviour. (a) An execution that ended (the engine's own end, not a person's or the supervisor's Stop) after a failed turn whose cause is `model_unavailable` keeps today's retry: resumed in the same native session on the same workspace (its files and checkpointed work kept) after the model backoff, as now. SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_RETRIES (default 3; a whole number from 1 to 20; any other value refused when the loop starts: it exits non-zero naming the setting and runs nothing) bounds those resumes: once a session has had that many resumes in a row of executions that ended this way with no model answer in between (a revived execution that made progress resets the count), its next such end is not resumed: the recovery records `execution.interrupted` {cause `model_unavailable`, path `final`, evidence including `retries`: the setting} for that end, once, and nothing revives it (a person or the supervisor may resume it). A failed turn whose engine stays at its prompt (no end) is retried as today, without this bound. (b) An execution that ended after a failed turn whose error is neither transient, nor a login (401, 403, `authentication_failed`), nor an exhausted context ("prompt is too long"), with no progress after that turn, is recorded `execution.interrupted` {cause `model_error` (a new cause: the store accepts it), path `final`, evidence: the failed turn's `event_id`, `status`, `error` and `text`} and never revived: no resume, no input, no new session. (c) The dispatcher tells the supervisor of each final model record once: one item in its digest, session the worker's, tag `<session> model-<execution id>` (`Escalation::tag`), its line naming the session, the execution, the cause and the status or the retries; news, told once (`Why::is_news`), never repeated on later passes. A person's or the supervisor's Stop still outranks every model cause.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/039.sh (read its header): a real loop with the supervisor, the dispatcher and three ephemeral workers on a fake engine whose turns follow a plan per agent, SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_BACKOFF_SECS=2 and SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_RETRIES=2: (1) a worker whose engine ends twice on a 529 and then works has its task reported, two `model_unavailable` interruptions and none `crashed` or `exited`, two `resume` revivals by the recovery each at least 2 s after the failed turn it retries, one native session, the third execution finding what the first two wrote, and no command from a person or the supervisor nor any `model-` digest about it; (2) a worker whose engine ends on a 400 runs once: one interruption `model_error final`, no revival within 20 s, and one digest tagged `<session> model-<execution>`, still one 15 s later; (3) a worker whose engine always ends on a 529 is resumed twice, its third end is recorded `model_unavailable final`, nothing revives it within 20 s, and the supervisor is told once; (4) with the loop stopped, `spawn loop` with SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_RETRIES 0, 21, -1 or `two` exits non-zero within 15 s naming it. It fails at (2) on the live main (a484b2c7): the 400's end is recorded `crashed`, path `resume`, and the worker is resumed at once.

What it saves. Every worker that ended on an outage or on a request the model will never accept is either back at work or in front of the supervisor, with nobody watching the pane: no ended worker resumed forever against a dead account (a worker whose engine stays at its prompt keeps today's unbounded wait: telling the supervisor after N live retries is a follow-up), and no worker crash-looping on an invalid request until a person notices. Fewer human interventions per agent-hour.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
